title: What Happens If You Hold In Your Pee?
sources: Piedmont Healthcare, 'How long is it safe to hold your urine?': a healthy bladder holds about 400-500 mL (roughly 2 cups); habitual holding can weaken the bladder muscle; rupture is rare
OSF HealthCare / Columbia Doctors (urology): urine that sits in the bladder stagnates and raises the risk of urinary tract infection; chronic overstretching can cause lasting damage
Michigan Medicine, 'Is it time to let go of holding it?': the bladder signals the brain as it fills; occasional holding is fine, a habit is not
Yang, Pham, Choo & Hu 2014, PNAS 111(33), 'Duration of urination does not change with body size': mammals above 3 kg empty their bladders in 21 ± 13 seconds

lines.text: What happens if you hold in your pee?
Your bladder is a stretchy bag that holds about two cups,
lines.caps: Your *bladder | is a *stretchy bag | that holds | about *two cups

lines.text: and as it fills, sensors in its wall start messaging your brain.
lines.caps: As it *fills | *sensors | in its wall | start *messaging | your *brain

lines.text: Hold it, and a ring of muscle clamps shut
while the bag keeps on stretching.
Once in a while, that's totally fine.
But make it a habit, and bacteria get time to multiply,
lines.caps: Make it a *habit | and *bacteria | get time | to *multiply

lines.text: and the muscle can stretch out and get weaker.
So when you've gotta go, just go.
Fun fact: almost every mammal bigger than a cat pees for about twenty-one seconds.
